# ECU menu

The ECU menu reads and flashes the ECU over CAN, the way the Trionic CAN Flasher does.
Like the Realtime menu it needs a file of the ECU open, and an interface set up in File → Settings → Common.
The progress shows in the status bar, and TxSuite won't close while it runs.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t8-manual"}
With File → Settings → T8 → Use Legion Bootloader on (the default) reading, flashing and recovering use the Legion bootloader, which only erases and writes the partitions that differ from the file.
:::

## ECU → Read ECU

Downloads the flash content from the connected ECU.
It will ask you where to store the binary file.

## ECU → Flash current file to ECU

Flashes the open file to the connected ECU.
Map viewers with unsaved changes are pointed out first, they are not in the file yet.
A wrong checksum is corrected first, or TxSuite offers to correct it when File → Settings → Common → Auto update checksum is off.
When it's done TxSuite says whether it worked.

A good check after flashing is to read the ECU back and compare the two files with Actions → Compare binary with other binary.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t8-manual"}
When the flash was erased but programming failed, TxSuite asks whether to attempt to recover the ECU with the same file.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t5-manual"}
## ECU → Get SRAM snapshot

Lets you create an SRAM snapshot from the ECU, a copy of its working memory, for later analysis or reference.
It needs a connection to the ECU, Realtime → Connect ECU.
In a project it goes into the project's Snapshots folder, otherwise TxSuite asks where to save it, proposing `Snapshot-<bin>-<time>.RAM`.

## ECU → Upload SRAM to ECU

This option allows you to upload a snapshot of the ECU's SRAM (working memory) back into the ECU.
This works like a sort of system restore point you can make.
Connect first with Realtime → Connect ECU, without a connection nothing happens.
TxSuite asks whether the maps should go into the binary file too.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t7-manual"}
## ECU → Get SRAM snapshot

Lets you download the ECU's working memory as a snapshot for comparing and backup.
In a project it goes into the project's Snapshots folder, otherwise next to the bin as `SRAM<time>.RAM`.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t8-manual"}
## ECU → Recover ECU

Brings back an ECU whose flashing failed halfway, by flashing a file through the bootloader.
It only takes a T8 binary whose checksum verifies.
:::
